body: .ok-planner/review/project.md:32 says 'read <id> [--opened <time>] marks every agent message read'; after this stage it records the read in the caller's git-ignored ledger and refuses with no name. The inputs are unchanged, so this stage left the entry; the issue-format item that edits project.md should restate it

artifact-definitions.md:244 defines unread as 'agent messages the owner has not yet read' and :253 gives a reply's read field as 'null until the owner reads it'; after this stage unread and unopened come from the reading person's ledger and new agent messages carry no read field (retired, accepted when present). The issue-format item that edits this file should restate both

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:103 (sprint step 5, The merge) summarizes the ownership test as 'a fix in the corpus or the harness settings sets the item to judgment' and does not name merge.md's new first bullet: a file the review script's OWNER_PATHS misclasses as corpus, where a corpus rule decides its class otherwise, merges as a defect in the list's file. The summary now undersells the test; the notes list no change to SKILL.md for B94.

The notes' call adds '# @decision: agent-revisions-reach-the-owner' above the EXECUTABLE_FILES row for scripts/issues in admin/true-up (line ~228); that file is outside this stage's files, so the citation is not written. word_diff carries no citation, per checks/materialized-standalone.

docs/integration-contract.md: the port-docs item has the repoint paragraph name .ok-planner/bin/port-block among the retired scripts; the contract is not a record to the review tool's ownership classes, so a true-up of this repository finds it as a caller, files retired-planner-port-block-caller-docs-integration-contract-md, and keeps .ok-planner/bin/port-block for as long as the paragraph names it (the same holds for line 304 and .ok-planner/review/project.md:47 until t26 lands).

docs/integration-contract.md:422, plugins/ok/CLAUDE.md:7, and plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/CLAUDE.md:16 list the core's modes (diagnose / true-up / wire-hooks / wire-env / resolve / amend) without the new read-only check-range mode; ADMINISTRATION.md and project.md name it.

.ok-planner/design/decisions/dashboard-started-by-skill.md Choice says the skill starts the service 'in the background of the owner's session'; the skill now starts it as a process detached from the session that outlives it. The words still read true of a detached background process, but the decision does not say the service outlives the session; no delta in this sprint amends it

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/core.md:148 says 'one an owner comment triage has not yet seen holds back'; the term is now 'a person's comment' (decision:anyone-may-rule, messages-carry-their-authors-name). Outside this stage's files.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/owner-list.md:48 says 'an update message the owner reads' and 'The owner's ruling, where one stands, is the owner's'; with several people working the intake the update reaches each person and the ruling is its author's. Outside this stage's files.

body: Reviewed /converge sprint mode's pass prompt against a scratch repo (git init; project root app/ trued up; code in app/main.py, shared/util.py, tools/gen.js; .ok-planner/config.json folders ["../shared","../tools"] written through true-up amend). review changed --base HEAD from app/ lists '../shared/util.py' and '../tools/gen.js', as the decision requires. sprint-pass.md line 17 tells a freshly dispatched pass agent to read 'each file's diff from `git diff --relative [BASE] -- <path>`'. --relative restricts git's output to the current directory, so for every file under a declared folder the diff is empty. Its sibling sprint-review.md line 20 says 'git diff [BASE] -- <path>' with no --relative. The story promises: 'so that no check the suite runs over my project misses code I own'; decision project-declares-its-folders: 'Every tool that lists or scopes the project's code reads that list: the review tool in every /converge mode'. saw: a reissued sprint-pass agent following the text reads no change for code in declared folders (and in a sprint's '## Paths outside the project root'). evidence: from app/: 'git diff --relative HEAD -- ../shared/util.py' printed nothing (exit 0, 0 lines); 'git diff HEAD -- ../shared/util.py' printed 'diff --git a/shared/util.py b/shared/util.py ... +# new narration line'; 'git diff --relative HEAD -- main.py' printed the diff for the root file.

body: Reviewed the sprint template's Completion contract (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:239-270) against /converge sprint's closing step (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:119) and drove the mechanical steps on a scratch project (true-up, a scratch sprint with -base.txt, review changed/checks/merges/fixes/verifies/backouts, a stuck defect whose backout restores a lint failure). The story promises: "done" means the same thing for every sprint. Saw: the contract gives two verdicts for one repository state. Item 2 (sprint-document.md:249-250) reads "The project builds, and the checks .ok-planner/review/config.json lists under checks pass on every file the change touched." Certification's last step (converge/SKILL.md:119) reads "A file that fails now becomes a stuck defect with the check's output, and the loop does not reopen." The goal rule (sprint-document.md:259-263) reads both "The goal is met when items 1-3 verify against the repository as it stands" and "A stuck defect listed in the return is the owner's to take up, and does not hold the goal open." A sprint whose certification ends with a stuck check failure (or any stuck defect whose backout leaves a check failing) fails item 2 and is, by the stuck clause, not held open: one checker reports done, another not done. Decision sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository's Choice repeats the stuck clause and names no exception to item 2. Evidence: scratch run, final check exec "closed t2 failed (exit 2)" with "plumbline/comment-hygiene: comment is not permitted" on src/calc.py:6 before the fix; defect i4 set stuck and backout t7 filed with brief "defect i4; fix tasks t5; before: src/calc.py 7d0077a".

Reviewed /converge sprint mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, prompts/sprint-pass.md, prompts/merge.md) against the sprint template's Completion contract (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:239-270); ran review owner on a scratch project, which classes the sprint's own applied delta .ok-planner/design/stories/subtract-numbers.md as "corpus". The story promises: when a sprint closes, the owner knows whether what was approved was delivered, and "done" means the same thing for every sprint. Saw: certification finds an unlanded delta and cannot land it, and the contract then has no outcome. Only after I ran 'true-up resolve citation-tags:.ok-planner/config.json' did the next true-up print 'CLEANUP OFFERED (ok-planner): port-range:.ok-planner/config.json'. ADMINISTRATION.md (port-range row) says the offer is 'Withheld while a config, config-key, or citation-tags offer stands', and a declined offer 'returns on the next true-up', so an owner who declines the citation tags is never asked for a range, while .ok-planner/bin/ports lease refuses with 'ports: .ok-planner/config.json declares no port names under ports, so there is nothing to lease; declare the names and a port_range through /ok' (exit 1), pointing at /ok, which then never asks. The story promises: a way to run isolated verification stacks side by side; decision port-range-chosen-at-true-up says 'Where a project publishes ports and declares no provisioning range, the true-up core offers one' and 'A project that publishes no ports gets no question'. Saw: a project that publishes ports and declares no range gets no question while the citation-tags offer stands, with no path to a range through /ok. Evidence: true-up output lines 'CLEANUP OFFERED (ok-planner): citation-tags:.ok-planner/config.json' and 'CLEANUP OFFERED (ok-planner): review-facts:.ok-planner/review/project.md' and nothing else; the lease refusal quoted above.

I reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md (drive mode steps 2 and 4), plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/review/seed/project.md, and 'review drive-command --help'. The seed tells the owner: 'stack-start leases the run's ports with .ok-planner/bin/ports lease <run-tag> before it builds the stack and starts it under the run's tag. stack-stop stops the stack, removes everything the run built under its tag ... and ends the lease with .ok-planner/bin/ports release <run-tag>.' The skill runs the two as separate exec tasks: step 2 'file one exec task that starts the stack with the command the section gives: tasks file --kind exec --key gate --command "<what review drive-command --role stack-start prints>"', step 4 'file and drain one exec task whose --command is what review drive-command --role stack-stop prints'. Nothing in the skill mints a run tag (it never calls .ok-planner/bin/run-tag) or hands one to either command, and drive-command fills only {name}, {folder}, and {service} ('usage: review drive-command [-h] --role {...} [--name NAME] [--folder FOLDER] [--service SERVICE]'). So stack-stop cannot learn the tag stack-start leased and built under except from a fixed place the project invents, and two /converge runs in one checkout write and read that one place: the second run's start replaces the first's tag, and the first run's stop then tears down the second run's stack and releases its lease. Drivers get no channel either for the ports the lease printed. The story promises: isolated verification stacks side by side, so that one verification run never disturbs another's results; decision per-run-artifact-tag says 'A verification run invokes it once, builds every artifact it verifies under the printed tag, and hands that one value to its verification path through one environment variable the project declares'. Saw: /converge, the verification run, mints no tag and passes none to its stack-start, stack-stop, or drivers. Evidence: the quoted SKILL.md steps; grep -i 'run-tag|run tag|RUN_TAG' over skills/converge/ and scripts/review returns no line that mints or substitutes a tag.

body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree (port_range 36879-37078, WEB_PORT declared through amend), I minted two run tags TA=run-bcbf45ff2db7 < TB=run-bfd84ae1a6d1, built one image under each (`docker build -t vlnab-a:$TA`, `-t vlnab-b:$TB`), and ran one container from TA's image with plain `docker run` (no compose label), then stopped it (`docker stop`, so it stays as an exited container, as `docker run` without --rm leaves it). TB is a dead run: no lease, no containers. I ran `.ok-planner/bin/ports` cleanup with a docker shim on PATH that passes every read through, passes `rm` through only for my two tags, and shifts `docker info` SystemTime two hours ahead so both tags are past the hour of grace. The story promises: each run's artifacts are removed once the run is over, so verification never fills the disk; run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run says the cleanup removes the container artifacts of every run tag that holds no lease, has no containers left, and has no artifact made in the last hour. Saw: `ports cleanup` exited 1 at TA and never reached TB: TB's image `vlnab-b:run-bfd84ae1a6d1` stayed. has_containers() looks only for containers labeled com.docker.compose.project=<tag>, so TA counts as container-less, `docker image rm` refuses, and the DockerFailed raise ends the loop in cleanup() over every later tag. The tags run in sorted order, so every later cleanup stops at the same tag for as long as that exited container exists, and no dead tag that sorts after it is ever cleaned. Evidence: stderr `{"kind": "PORTS.RUN.FAILED", "error": "DockerFailed", "message": "docker image rm vlnab-a:run-bcbf45ff2db7 exited 1: Error response from daemon: conflict: unable to delete vlnab-a:run-bcbf45ff2db7 (must be forced) - container f6c6a9cccd88 is using its referenced image c8ec6ee59022"}`, exit status 1 (the same with the container running and with it exited); afterwards `docker image ls` still listed `vlnab-b:run-bfd84ae1a6d1` and `vlnab-a:run-bcbf45ff2db7`. Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports cleanup() / remove_artifacts() / has_containers().

In the same scratch project I minted T3=run-62dc11c74373 and built one image under it with two tags, `docker build -t vlnab-arch:$T3-amd64 -t vlnab-plain:$T3`, then ran `.ok-planner/bin/ports cleanup` with the docker shim (two hours shifted, rm passed through for T3 only). The story promises: each run's artifacts are removed once the run is over; the rules layer (ok-planner-cheatsheet.md, Per-run artifacts) tells the owner to build every artifact a run verifies under its tag, and says cleanup removes the container artifacts of every dead run tag; it never says an image tag must equal the run tag exactly. Saw: cleanup printed `removed: run-62dc11c74373 (1 image(s), 0 volume(s), 0 network(s))`, reporting the run cleaned, yet `vlnab-arch:run-62dc11c74373-amd64` stayed: run_artifacts() takes an image only when its tag matches ^run-[0-9a-f]{12}$ whole or its repository starts with the run tag. On this machine `docker image ls` lists 28 images of another project tagged this way (`gridiq-allinone:run-d61aae7a593d-amd64` 6.24GB, `gridiq-grafana:run-d61aae7a593d-amd64` 992MB, `gridiq-keycloak:run-1a556e12fd9a-amd64` 247MB, ...), two to four weeks old; my shimmed cleanup listed none of them as due (no WOULD-REMOVE line), and a probe of run_artifacts() returned only my own tags. Evidence: the `removed:` line above; `docker image ls` after the cleanup: `vlnab-arch:run-62dc11c74373-amd64`; `docker system df`: Images 34.71GB, 16.91GB reclaimable. Possible not-owed reading for the merge: `ports --help` says `each image tagged with the run tag`, which an owner could read as exact; the rules layer an agent wires the stack from does not say it.

I reviewed /converge's drive steps in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md (In drive mode, steps 2 and 4; Loop 2 step 6; In sprint mode step 4) against the story and run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run. Diverging text, step 2: `Where it fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds.` Step 4, the only place the run files the stack-stop task and the port cleanup, is skipped on that branch, so a stack start that failed after it leased its ports and built its images (a failed health check, a bind failure past the retry budget) leaves that run's artifacts and lease, and the run runs no cleanup at all. Loop 2 step 6 (confirm) starts the stack again and says nothing of a failed start either. The decision says: `The run's stack stop removes everything the run built under its tag, whether the run passed or failed`, and among its alternatives rejects removal at the stack stop alone because `a run that crashes before its stack stops leaves its artifacts on disk for good`; the seed project.md says stack-stop `removes everything the run built under its tag, whether the run passed or failed`. A run whose start failed is a failed run the text never stops: its artifacts of other kinds than containers stay until a person removes them, and its container artifacts wait for some later run's cleanup.

I reviewed /audit (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md) and the measurement auditor prompt it reads (skills/_shared/implementation-auditor.md, the story and assumption auditors) against the story and run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run. audit/SKILL.md, Port cleanup, says: `It frees and removes only what is due; an experiment's own stack stop removes what its run built.` The auditor prompt never tells an auditor or an experiment to build under a run tag, to stop a stack it starts, or to remove what it built: under `Obtaining the deployment state an experiment needs` it says `3. **Provision a second deployment** only when neither works` and gives no step that tears that deployment down; `grep -n -i 'run tag\|run-tag\|stack stop\|teardown'` over implementation-auditor.md finds no instruction of the kind (its only `teardown` is `the project's own teardown` used to reset). The decision says: `A run's artifacts end with the run: the run tag's life is mint, build, verify, remove`, and names the audit's experiment runs as runs whose artifacts the cleanup must reach. The audit runs `ports cleanup` once, right after the measurement track drains, when everything its experiments built is inside the hour of grace, so nothing a provisioned deployment of this audit built is removed by this run: container artifacts wait for a later cleanup, and other artifacts stay for good.

Unlisted behavior change behind build call i82. Changed site: admin/true-up::stripped splits the decoded bytes with re.split(r'(?<=
)') and compares line.rstrip('
') against '## <name>'. In a story or decision file with CRLF line endings each heading line is '## Proof', so it never matches: found stays empty, retired_section_files skips the file, strip_story_sections/strip_decision_proofs strip nothing, diagnose reports nothing, and retired_layout_offers offers nothing. At the base (git show 119169e:./plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge), read_owner opened the file with universal newlines, so the regex '
## (Falsifier|Proof|Acceptance)

body: decision:port-range-chosen-at-true-up Choice: 'Where a project publishes ports and declares no provisioning range, the true-up core offers one ... A declined offer returns on the next true-up.' admin/true-up::offers runs port_range_offer only when config_offers() is empty ('config_held = config_offers(); out.extend(config_held); if not config_held: out.extend(port_range_offer())'), and port_range_offer returns [] when .ok-planner/config.json does not exist ('if lint_config_path() != planner_config or not os.path.isfile(planner_config): return []'). config_offers returns a citation-tags offer whenever the config declares no @subject:/@practice: (or design) tags, and with no config file at all; ADMINISTRATION.md says a citation-tags no 'is a valid state, recorded as declined; the next run offers it again', and the config-key offer for a kept retired 'checks' key behaves the same. Trigger: a project whose compose file publishes ${WEB_PORT:-8080} (or whose ports array names a port) and whose owner declines the citation-tags (or config-key) offer, or that has no config file and declines the citation-tags offer. Every diagnose and true-up then prints no port-range block, so the owner is never asked for a range, and .ok-planner/bin/ports lease refuses forever ('declares no port_range ... run /ok, which suggests one') although /ok never offers it: the refusal's own remedy fails (also A9). The withholding exists to keep two drafts of one file apart in one pass; it stands for good once the other offer is declined. Scope: caused by this sprint (new code).

ports cleanup -> ::cleanup -> for tag in sorted(found): ... ::has_containers(docker, tag) checks only containers labelled com.docker.compose.project=<tag> -> ::remove_artifacts -> ::docker_out(docker, [kind, 'rm', name], absent_ok=True). docker_out raises DockerFailed for every stderr line not matching DOCKER_ABSENT ('no such (image|volume|network)|network \S+ not found'). An image tagged run-<hex> (or a run's volume or network) still referenced by a container that carries no compose label for that tag (a 'docker run' container an experiment or a run started from the run's image, running or stopped) answers 'conflict: unable to remove repository reference ... container ... is using its referenced image' (or 'volume is in use', 'has active endpoints'), so docker_out raises, the owner frame emits PORTS.RUN.FAILED and exits 1, and every tag sorted after it is never cleaned. The same tag sorts first again on every later cleanup, so one in-use artifact blocks removal of every other dead run's artifacts for good while each run reports a failed cleanup: the periodic work stops making progress (A5), and decision:run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run ('removes the container artifacts ... of every run tag that holds no lease, has no containers left') is not met for the other tags. Scope: caused (new code).

decision:port-range-chosen-at-true-up Choice: 'Where a project publishes ports and declares no provisioning range, the true-up core offers one ... A declined offer returns on the next true-up.' admin/true-up::offers runs port_range_offer only when config_offers() is empty ('config_held = config_offers(); out.extend(config_held); if not config_held: out.extend(port_range_offer())'), and port_range_offer returns [] when .ok-planner/config.json does not exist ('if lint_config_path() != planner_config or not os.path.isfile(planner_config): return []'). config_offers returns a citation-tags offer whenever the config declares no @subject:/@practice: (or design) tags, and with no config file at all; ADMINISTRATION.md says a citation-tags no 'is a valid state, recorded as declined; the next run offers it again', and the config-key offer for a kept retired 'checks' key behaves the same. Trigger: a project whose compose file publishes ${WEB_PORT:-8080} (or whose ports array names a port) and whose owner declines the citation-tags (or config-key) offer, or that has no config file and declines the citation-tags offer. Every diagnose and true-up then prints no port-range block, so the owner is never asked for a range, and .ok-planner/bin/ports lease refuses forever ('declares no port_range ... run /ok, which suggests one') although /ok never offers it: the refusal's own remedy fails (also A9). The withholding exists to keep two drafts of one file apart in one pass; it stands for good once the other offer is declined. Scope: caused by this sprint (new code).

The same tag sorts first again on every later cleanup, so one in-use artifact blocks removal of every other dead run's artifacts for good while each run reports a failed cleanup: the periodic work stops making progress (A5), and decision:run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run ('removes the container artifacts ... of every run tag that holds no lease, has no containers left') is not met for the other tags. Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports:cleanup, has_containers, remove_artifacts. What the code does: has_containers(docker, tag) counts only containers labeled com.docker.compose.project=<tag>, so a run tag whose image a plain 'docker run' container uses (running or exited) counts as container-less; remove_artifacts then runs 'docker image rm', which the daemon refuses, docker_out raises DockerFailed, and the raise ends cleanup's 'for tag in sorted(found)' loop. Trigger: any container outside compose that uses an image tagged run-<12 hex>. Harm (A5): the periodic cleanup stops at that tag on every run for as long as the container exists, and no dead tag that sorts after it is ever cleaned, while the command looks like it works for earlier tags; decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run says the cleanup removes the artifacts of every run tag that 'has no containers left'. Evidence: stderr '{"kind": "PORTS.RUN.FAILED", "error": "DockerFailed", "message": "docker image rm vlnab-a:run-bcbf45ff2db7 exited 1: ... conflict: unable to delete ... container f6c6a9cccd88 is using its referenced image ..."}', exit 1; afterwards 'docker image ls' still listed vlnab-b:run-bfd84ae1a6d1 (a dead run with no lease and no containers). New file in this sprint's change. From failure i18.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md 'In drive mode' step 2 ('Where it fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds') and Loop 2 step 6 (confirm starts the stack and says nothing of a failed start). What the text does: a stack start that fails jumps to Loop 2 and skips step 4, the only place the run files stack-stop, the instance and resource stops, and the port cleanup this sprint added. Trigger: a stack-start that leased its ports and built its images, then failed (a failed health check, a bind failure past the retry budget). Harm (A8): decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run: 'The run's stack stop removes everything the run built under its tag, whether the run passed or failed'; the seed facts repeat it. The failed run's lease and artifacts stay, artifacts other than containers stay for good, and the run runs no cleanup, contrary to this sprint's work item 'file and drain one exec task running .ok-planner/bin/ports cleanup wherever review drive-stack printed stack'. Evidence: SKILL.md:77 step 2 quoted above; SKILL.md:79 step 4 holds the stop and the cleanup. In scope: the change added the cleanup to step 4 and the decision, and the failed-start path makes that outcome fail. From failure i20.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/SKILL.md: the phase 2 reviewer's thin-discovery request format is concept-only ('### <affected-concept-slug>', '- Promote new concept: <name | none>', SKILL.md:543-546), while the back-edge extractor is written for any kind ('Each names the affected artifact kind and slug', SKILL.md:675-676; it edits a story's statement or a decision's Choice) and speaks of 'Promote new artifact' (SKILL.md:670-671); the orchestrator fills the request between them, so a concept promotion still reaches the extractor, but no thin story or decision can be requested. Reading 1: the story promises only autonomous extraction into the catalogs, so a concept-only back-edge is enough. Reading 2: the extractor's own text shows the back-edge is meant to sharpen stories and decisions too, so the reviewer's format should name a kind and the field should read the same on both sides. The story bootstrap-design-corpus does not say which.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports:run_artifacts takes an image as a run's only when its tag is exactly run-<12 hex> or its repository starts with the run tag, so an image tagged run-<12 hex>-amd64 (a suffixed run tag) is never removed, while the cleanup reports the run as removed. Reading 1: 'every image tagged with the run tag' (sprint work item; ports --help) means the exact tag, and a project that suffixes the tag builds outside the rule. Reading 2: decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run ('removes the container artifacts ... of every run tag') and the rules layer, which never says an image tag must equal the run tag, cover any tag that carries the run tag, so suffixed tags (seen on this machine: 28 images of another project, e.g. gridiq-allinone:run-d61aae7a593d-amd64, 6.24GB) should be removed too; widening the match also widens what a cleanup may delete across projects on the machine. Neither the story nor the decision decides it.

Sprint certification's alignment pass reports a delta not landed (C3), and plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md 'In sprint mode' step 5 and prompts/merge.md route every corpus fix to judgment, so certification cannot land the sprint's own approved delta; contract item 1 ('Every corpus matches every delta above, applied verbatim') then stays unmet, and the goal rule exempts only a stuck defect, so a goal checker either loops or ignores item 1. Reading 1: landing an approved sprint's own delta verbatim is a change 'through a sprint's deltas', which the decision allows, so certification's fixer may land it. Reading 2: the decision's 'A defect whose fix lies in the corpus ... goes to the intake as a judgment issue' binds every /converge run, so the contract's goal rule must exempt a judgment item as it exempts a stuck one. The corpus does not decide which.

In a scratch git project (mktemp -d, git init) holding stack/compose.yaml that publishes "8080:80" and "${DB_PORT:-5432}:5432", I ran plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up (no argument), twice, with no .ok-planner/config.json. Neither run offered a port range: its only CLEANUP OFFERED blocks were citation-tags:.ok-planner/config.json and review-facts:.ok-planner/review/project.md (grep -c port-range on the output: 0), although .ok-planner/bin/plumbline compose-ports printed {"file":"stack/compose.yaml","line":5,"variables":[],"port":8080} and {"file":"stack/compose.yaml","line":9,"variables":["DB_PORT"],"port":5432}. Only after I ran 'true-up resolve citation-tags:.ok-planner/config.json' did the next true-up print 'CLEANUP OFFERED (ok-planner): port-range:.ok-planner/config.json'. ADMINISTRATION.md (port-range row) says the offer is 'Withheld while a config, config-key, or citation-tags offer stands', and a declined offer 'returns on the next true-up', so an owner who declines the citation tags is never asked for a range, while .ok-planner/bin/ports lease refuses with 'ports: .ok-planner/config.json declares no port names under ports, so there is nothing to lease; declare the names and a port_range through /ok' (exit 1), pointing at /ok, which then never asks. The story promises: a way to run isolated verification stacks side by side; decision port-range-chosen-at-true-up says 'Where a project publishes ports and declares no provisioning range, the true-up core offers one' and 'A project that publishes no ports gets no question'. Saw: a project that publishes ports and declares no range gets no question while the citation-tags offer stands, with no path to a range through /ok. Evidence: true-up output lines 'CLEANUP OFFERED (ok-planner): citation-tags:.ok-planner/config.json' and 'CLEANUP OFFERED (ok-planner): review-facts:.ok-planner/review/project.md' and nothing else; the lease refusal quoted above.

I reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md (drive mode steps 2 and 4), plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/review/seed/project.md, and 'review drive-command --help'. The seed tells the owner: 'stack-start leases the run's ports with .ok-planner/bin/ports lease <run-tag> before it builds the stack and starts it under the run's tag. stack-stop stops the stack, removes everything the run built under its tag ... and ends the lease with .ok-planner/bin/ports release <run-tag>.' The skill runs the two as separate exec tasks: step 2 'file one exec task that starts the stack with the command the section gives: tasks file --kind exec --key gate --command "<what review drive-command --role stack-start prints>"', step 4 'file and drain one exec task whose --command is what review drive-command --role stack-stop prints'. Nothing in the skill mints a run tag (it never calls .ok-planner/bin/run-tag) or hands one to either command, and drive-command fills only {name}, {folder}, and {service} ('usage: review drive-command [-h] --role {...} [--name NAME] [--folder FOLDER] [--service SERVICE]'). So stack-stop cannot learn the tag stack-start leased and built under except from a fixed place the project invents, and two /converge runs in one checkout write and read that one place: the second run's start replaces the first's tag, and the first run's stop then tears down the second run's stack and releases its lease. Drivers get no channel either for the ports the lease printed. The story promises: isolated verification stacks side by side, so that one verification run never disturbs another's results; decision per-run-artifact-tag says 'A verification run invokes it once, builds every artifact it verifies under the printed tag, and hands that one value to its verification path through one environment variable the project declares'. Saw: /converge, the verification run, mints no tag and passes none to its stack-start, stack-stop, or drivers. Evidence: the quoted SKILL.md steps; grep -i 'run-tag|run tag|RUN_TAG' over skills/converge/ and scripts/review returns no line that mints or substitutes a tag.

In a scratch project trued up from the working tree (port_range 36879-37078, WEB_PORT declared through amend), I minted two run tags TA=run-bcbf45ff2db7 < TB=run-bfd84ae1a6d1, built one image under each (`docker build -t vlnab-a:$TA`, `-t vlnab-b:$TB`), and ran one container from TA's image with plain `docker run` (no compose label), then stopped it (`docker stop`, so it stays as an exited container, as `docker run` without --rm leaves it). TB is a dead run: no lease, no containers. I ran `.ok-planner/bin/ports` cleanup with a docker shim on PATH that passes every read through, passes `rm` through only for my two tags, and shifts `docker info` SystemTime two hours ahead so both tags are past the hour of grace. The story promises: each run's artifacts are removed once the run is over, so verification never fills the disk; run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run says the cleanup removes the container artifacts of every run tag that holds no lease, has no containers left, and has no artifact made in the last hour. Saw: `ports cleanup` exited 1 at TA and never reached TB: TB's image `vlnab-b:run-bfd84ae1a6d1` stayed. has_containers() looks only for containers labeled com.docker.compose.project=<tag>, so TA counts as container-less, `docker image rm` refuses, and the DockerFailed raise ends the loop in cleanup() over every later tag. The tags run in sorted order, so every later cleanup stops at the same tag for as long as that exited container exists, and no dead tag that sorts after it is ever cleaned. Evidence: stderr `{"kind": "PORTS.RUN.FAILED", "error": "DockerFailed", "message": "docker image rm vlnab-a:run-bcbf45ff2db7 exited 1: Error response from daemon: conflict: unable to delete vlnab-a:run-bcbf45ff2db7 (must be forced) - container f6c6a9cccd88 is using its referenced image c8ec6ee59022"}`, exit status 1 (the same with the container running and with it exited); afterwards `docker image ls` still listed `vlnab-b:run-bfd84ae1a6d1` and `vlnab-a:run-bcbf45ff2db7`. Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports cleanup() / remove_artifacts() / has_containers().

I reviewed /converge's drive steps in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md (In drive mode, steps 2 and 4; Loop 2 step 6; In sprint mode step 4) against the story and run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run. Diverging text, step 2: `Where it fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds.` Step 4, the only place the run files the stack-stop task and the port cleanup, is skipped on that branch, so a stack start that failed after it leased its ports and built its images (a failed health check, a bind failure past the retry budget) leaves that run's artifacts and lease, and the run runs no cleanup at all. Loop 2 step 6 (confirm) starts the stack again and says nothing of a failed start either. The decision says: `The run's stack stop removes everything the run built under its tag, whether the run passed or failed`, and among its alternatives rejects removal at the stack stop alone because `a run that crashes before its stack stops leaves its artifacts on disk for good`; the seed project.md says stack-stop `removes everything the run built under its tag, whether the run passed or failed`. A run whose start failed is a failed run the text never stops: its artifacts of other kinds than containers stay until a person removes them, and its container artifacts wait for some later run's cleanup.

body: Reviewed the sprint template's Completion contract (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:239-270) against /converge sprint's closing step (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:119) and drove the mechanical steps on a scratch project (true-up, a scratch sprint with -base.txt, review changed/checks/merges/fixes/verifies/backouts, a stuck defect whose backout restores a lint failure). body: Reviewed /converge sprint mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, prompts/sprint-pass.md, prompts/merge.md) against the sprint template's Completion contract (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:239-270); ran review owner on a scratch project, which classes the sprint's own applied delta .ok-planner/design/stories/subtract-numbers.md as "corpus". The alignment pass reports C3 "A corpus delta whose artifact ... does not match the delta's final-form body byte for byte" (_sprint/shared.md:276). converge/SKILL.md:103 then routes it away from the fix loop: "it applies the ownership test of merge step 3a to the file each fix lies in, as in every mode, even where the sprint's change edited the file or a delta names the artifact: a fix in the corpus or the harness settings sets the item to judgment" (same in prompts/merge.md:62). note: The driver expected certification to land an unlanded delta (C3) so contract item 1 can be met; converge SKILL.md sprint step 5 and prompts/merge.md route every corpus fix to judgment. The corpus does not decide whether certification may land its own sprint's approved delta (decision runs-fix-what-the-project-owns: corpus changes 'only through a sprint's deltas', yet 'A defect whose fix lies in the corpus ... goes to the intake as a judgment issue') or whether the goal rule must exempt a judgment item as it exempts a stuck one (decision sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository names only stuck). body: Reviewed /plan-sprint's issue walk and ran the script it calls against a scratch project (git init + true-up, design corpus with concept:widget, story:frobnicate-widgets, decision:blue-widgets). body: Reviewed /plan-sprint's Sign-off step and the compliance reviewer prompt it dispatches (skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md, {{DESIGN-DOC-COMPLIANCE-REVIEWER-PROMPT}}). The two texts give different dispositions for a judgment finding on the sprint's own deltas. The prompt, line 50-51, tells the reviewer: 'The caller fixes mechanical findings and files judgment findings to the intake.' SKILL.md '7. Sign-off' says: 'Walk with the owner only a judgment finding that meets {{OWNER-QUESTION-TEST}}; settle every other one as a call the rules decide, and list it at Approval. Re-dispatch until clean.' The story promises 'a signed-off, self-sufficient sprint, so that any executor can realize my intent without ... deciding my open questions for me'; a judgment finding on a delta filed to the intake instead would let the owner approve a delta whose compliance question is still open, and leave it for the executor or a later sprint. Saw: the reviewer's prompt still states the intake disposition the session no longer follows, so a session that takes the dispatched prompt's description at its word, or a reviewer that shapes its judgment findings as intake filings, diverges from the Sign-off rule. Evidence: grep -n 'files judgment findings to the intake' design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md -> '51:  mechanical findings and files judgment findings to the intake. Do'.
note: The driver expected the compliance reviewer prompt's description of its caller to match /plan-sprint's Sign-off. The story plan-a-sprint promises a signed-off, self-sufficient sprint; SKILL.md '7. Sign-off' is the session's own rule for disposing judgment findings and governs it, and the reviewer's sentence ('The caller fixes mechanical findings and files judgment findings to the intake. Do not triage.') changes nothing the reviewer reports, so no owner question leaves the sprint through it. The corpus decides this: nothing the story promises fails.

body: Reviewed the discover-design skill source (SKILL.md, the artifact-definitions and dispatch-discipline blocks it transcludes) and ran its scripts against a scratch project trued up from the working tree: issues list, issues file --from - (kind discover; a duplicate open id refused with exit 2), issues list --artifact, issues show --json, python3 .ok-planner/bin/catalog-toc and --check, and the step 9 archive moves (git mv for a tracked note, mv for an untracked one, rmdir of the emptied _discover/). All of that works. The divergence is in the back-edge's hand-off format. The phase 2 reviewer writes each thin discovery request as '### <affected-concept-slug>' with the field '- Promote new concept: <name | none>' (SKILL.md:543-546). The back-edge extractor is told 'add a new artifact file only where the original request authorized "Promote new artifact"' (SKILL.md:669-671) and that each request 'names the affected artifact kind and slug' (SKILL.md:675-676), and it edits 'a story's Story statement; a decision's Choice, Rationale, or Alternatives' (SKILL.md:683-686). The reviewer's format never names a kind or carries a 'Promote new artifact' field, so a story or decision cannot be the target of a request, and a literal reading of the extractor finds no authorization for a concept the reviewer asked to promote. The story promises: the as-is model extracted autonomously into durable catalogs, with owner attention spent only on genuine ambiguities. Saw: the one back-edge that sharpens thin artifacts cannot target stories or decisions, and its promotion field is named differently on the two sides, so a load-bearing artifact the reviewer flagged as thin stays thin or unwritten. Evidence: SKILL.md:546 'Promote new concept: <name | none>'; SKILL.md:670-671 'only where the original request authorized "Promote new artifact"'; SKILL.md:675-676 'Each names the affected artifact kind and slug'.
note: The driver expected the discover-design back-edge to reach thin stories and decisions and to read its promotion field the same on both sides. The story bootstrap-design-corpus promises autonomous extraction into the durable catalogs and owner attention only on genuine ambiguities; it promises no back-edge per artifact kind, and the orchestrator fills each request's kind and promotion authorization between the reviewer and the extractor, so a requested concept promotion still reaches the extractor. The corpus does not decide whether stories and decisions should get a back-edge: question recorded as call i46.

body: In the same scratch project I minted T3=run-62dc11c74373 and built one image under it with two tags, `docker build -t vlnab-arch:$T3-amd64 -t vlnab-plain:$T3`, then ran `.ok-planner/bin/ports cleanup` with the docker shim (two hours shifted, rm passed through for T3 only). The story promises: each run's artifacts are removed once the run is over; the rules layer (ok-planner-cheatsheet.md, Per-run artifacts) tells the owner to build every artifact a run verifies under its tag, and says cleanup removes the container artifacts of every dead run tag; it never says an image tag must equal the run tag exactly. Saw: cleanup printed `removed: run-62dc11c74373 (1 image(s), 0 volume(s), 0 network(s))`, reporting the run cleaned, yet `vlnab-arch:run-62dc11c74373-amd64` stayed: run_artifacts() takes an image only when its tag matches ^run-[0-9a-f]{12}$ whole or its repository starts with the run tag. On this machine `docker image ls` lists 28 images of another project tagged this way (`gridiq-allinone:run-d61aae7a593d-amd64` 6.24GB, `gridiq-grafana:run-d61aae7a593d-amd64` 992MB, `gridiq-keycloak:run-1a556e12fd9a-amd64` 247MB, ...), two to four weeks old; my shimmed cleanup listed none of them as due (no WOULD-REMOVE line), and a probe of run_artifacts() returned only my own tags. Evidence: the `removed:` line above; `docker image ls` after the cleanup: `vlnab-arch:run-62dc11c74373-amd64`; `docker system df`: Images 34.71GB, 16.91GB reclaimable. Possible not-owed reading for the merge: `ports --help` says `each image tagged with the run tag`, which an owner could read as exact; the rules layer an agent wires the stack from does not say it.
note: The driver expected ports cleanup to remove an image tagged run-<12 hex>-amd64. The sprint's work item and ports --help say 'every image tagged with the run tag', which reads as the exact tag, and decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run says 'every run tag' without saying whether a suffixed tag carries it; the 'removed: run-62dc11c74373 (1 image(s) ...)' line counts what it did remove. body: I reviewed /audit (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md) and the measurement auditor prompt it reads (skills/_shared/implementation-auditor.md, the story and assumption auditors) against the story and run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run. audit/SKILL.md, Port cleanup, says: `It frees and removes only what is due; an experiment's own stack stop removes what its run built.` The auditor prompt never tells an auditor or an experiment to build under a run tag, to stop a stack it starts, or to remove what it built: under `Obtaining the deployment state an experiment needs` it says `3. **Provision a second deployment** only when neither works` and gives no step that tears that deployment down; `grep -n -i 'run tag\|run-tag\|stack stop\|teardown'` over implementation-auditor.md finds no instruction of the kind (its only `teardown` is `the project's own teardown` used to reset). body: Reviewed plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md (with plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md and the true-up core it drives) against the story; read the installed plugin registry read-only. The story promises: one deliberate act brings the project's whole suite presence to the current suite version; the skill's own opening says 'One command brings the suite current in this project: update the installed user-scoped plugins, ... then administer it in one pass'. Saw: step 1 runs 'claude plugin update <name>@ok-plugins   # for each installed ok-plugin, including ok itself', and step 4 then drives every core call from '<payload>', which 'Resolving the payload' fixes as '${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-plugins/ok}/families/ok-planner'. The installed front door lives at a versioned path: ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json reads 'ok@ok-plugins ... "installPath": "/Users/patrick/.claude/plugins/cache/ok-plugins/ok/25.4.0", "version": "25.4.0"'. An update installs the new release at a new versioned path, while the running session's CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT still names the old one until /reload-plugins, so the same pass trues the project up from the payload the update just superseded, and the report's carried column shows the old version. The skill tells the owner only 'Plugin updates take effect after /reload-plugins or a session restart', and never that the project was trued up to the pre-update version and needs /ok again after the reload (or that the pass must stop after step 1 when anything moved). Where the update removes the old cache folder, the step 4 commands name a payload that no longer exists. Either way one /ok does not bring the project to the current suite version whenever step 1 updates ok.
note: Site: plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md step 1 ('claude plugin update <name>@ok-plugins # for each installed ok-plugin, including ok itself') with 'Resolving the payload' ('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-plugins/ok}/families/ok-planner'). Entry: A3 (an /ok user whose step 1 updates ok gets the project trued up from the superseded payload, since the session's CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT names the old versioned install path until /reload-plugins; the skill says only that plugin changes take effect after a reload and never that /ok must run again). Evidence: ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json reads 'installPath: .../cache/ok-plugins/ok/25.4.0', a versioned path an update replaces. Outside the sprint: step 1 and the payload resolution stand the same at base 119169e; the sprint's edits to the file rename converge to true-up and do not reach them.

brief:
fix round 1; defects i35 i44
- i35: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports:cleanup -> :remove_artifacts -> :docker_out. What the code does: cleanup walks 'for tag in sorted(found)', skips a tag only where has_containers finds a container labelled com.docker.compose.project=<tag>, then remove_artifacts runs 'docker_out(docker, [kind, "rm", name], absent_ok=True)' for each image, volume, and network. docker_out raises DockerFailed for every stderr line DOCKER_ABSENT ('no such (image|volume|network)|network \S+ not found') does not match. Trigger: an image tagged run-<hex> (or a run's volume or network) still in use by a container that carries no compose label for that tag, such as a 'docker run' container an experiment started from the run's image, running or stopped; docker answers 'conflict: unable to remove repository reference ... is using its referenced image' (or 'volume is in use', 'has active endpoints'). Harm (A5): DockerFailed reaches the owner frame, which emits PORTS.RUN.FAILED and exits 1, and every tag sorted after the in-use one is never cleaned; that tag sorts at the same place on every later cleanup, so one in-use artifact stops every later cleanup from removing any other dead run's artifacts, while each drive and audit records a failed cleanup. decision:run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run Choice ('also removes the container artifacts ... of every run tag that holds no lease, has no containers left, and has no artifact made in the last hour') is not met for the other tags. Caused by the change (new code). Reports: i28.
- i44: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports:cleanup, has_containers, remove_artifacts. What the code does: has_containers(docker, tag) counts only containers labeled com.docker.compose.project=<tag>, so a run tag whose image a plain 'docker run' container uses (running or exited) counts as container-less; remove_artifacts then runs 'docker image rm', which the daemon refuses, docker_out raises DockerFailed, and the raise ends cleanup's 'for tag in sorted(found)' loop. Trigger: any container outside compose that uses an image tagged run-<12 hex>. Harm (A5): the periodic cleanup stops at that tag on every run for as long as the container exists, and no dead tag that sorts after it is ever cleaned, while the command looks like it works for earlier tags; decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run says the cleanup removes the artifacts of every run tag that 'has no containers left'. Evidence: stderr '{"kind": "PORTS.RUN.FAILED", "error": "DockerFailed", "message": "docker image rm vlnab-a:run-bcbf45ff2db7 exited 1: ... conflict: unable to delete ... container f6c6a9cccd88 is using its referenced image ..."}', exit 1; afterwards 'docker image ls' still listed vlnab-b:run-bfd84ae1a6d1 (a dead run with no lease and no containers). New file in this sprint's change. From failure i18.

brief:
fix round 1; defects i43 i45
- i43: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md 'In drive mode' steps 2 and 4 and Loop 2 step 6; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review drive-command (fills only {name}, {folder}, {service}); plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/review/seed/project.md '## Drive commands' ('stack-start leases the run's ports with .ok-planner/bin/ports lease <run-tag> ... stack-stop ... ends the lease with .ok-planner/bin/ports release <run-tag>'). What the text does: this sprint's seed tells the owner to write stack-start and stack-stop around one run tag, but /converge runs them as two separate exec tasks, mints no tag (never calls .ok-planner/bin/run-tag), and hands none to either command or to the drivers; drive-command has no placeholder for it. Trigger: any drive with a stack, and two /converge runs in one checkout. Harm (A3): stack-stop cannot learn the tag stack-start leased and built under except from a fixed place the project invents, so it cannot release the lease or remove the run's artifacts by tag; with two runs at once, the second start overwrites that place and the first run's stop tears down the second's stack and releases its lease, the collision the story exists to prevent. Story concurrent-stacks-without-port-collisions; decision per-run-artifact-tag: 'A verification run invokes it once, builds every artifact it verifies under the printed tag, and hands that one value to its verification path'. Evidence: 'usage: review drive-command [-h] --role {...} [--name NAME] [--folder FOLDER] [--service SERVICE]'; grep -i 'run-tag|run tag' over skills/converge/ and scripts/review finds no line that mints or passes a tag. In scope: the seed's <run-tag> wording is this sprint's change. From failure i16.
- i45: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md 'In drive mode' step 2 ('Where it fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds') and Loop 2 step 6 (confirm starts the stack and says nothing of a failed start). What the text does: a stack start that fails jumps to Loop 2 and skips step 4, the only place the run files stack-stop, the instance and resource stops, and the port cleanup this sprint added. Trigger: a stack-start that leased its ports and built its images, then failed (a failed health check, a bind failure past the retry budget). Harm (A8): decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run: 'The run's stack stop removes everything the run built under its tag, whether the run passed or failed'; the seed facts repeat it. The failed run's lease and artifacts stay, artifacts other than containers stay for good, and the run runs no cleanup, contrary to this sprint's work item 'file and drain one exec task running .ok-planner/bin/ports cleanup wherever review drive-stack printed stack'. Evidence: SKILL.md:77 step 2 quoted above; SKILL.md:79 step 4 holds the stop and the cleanup. In scope: the change added the cleanup to step 4 and the decision, and the failed-start path makes that outcome fail. From failure i20.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports:cleanup -> remove_artifacts: a docker refusal that no container causes (an image with dependent child images, or a container made between the in-use check and the rm) still raises DockerFailed out of the 'for tag in sorted(found)' loop, so every tag sorted after it stays uncleaned on every later cleanup (A5). The fix for i35/i44 covers the container-use case only.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports:cleanup, has_containers, remove_artifacts. What the code does: has_containers(docker, tag) counts only containers labeled com.docker.compose.project=<tag>, so a run tag whose image a plain 'docker run' container uses (running or exited) counts as container-less; remove_artifacts then runs 'docker image rm', which the daemon refuses, docker_out raises DockerFailed, and the raise ends cleanup's 'for tag in sorted(found)' loop. Trigger: any container outside compose that uses an image tagged run-<12 hex>. Harm (A5): the periodic cleanup stops at that tag on every run for as long as the container exists, and no dead tag that sorts after it is ever cleaned, while the command looks like it works for earlier tags; decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run says the cleanup removes the artifacts of every run tag that 'has no containers left'. Evidence: stderr '{"kind": "PORTS.RUN.FAILED", "error": "DockerFailed", "message": "docker image rm vlnab-a:run-bcbf45ff2db7 exited 1: ... conflict: unable to delete ... container f6c6a9cccd88 is using its referenced image ..."}', exit 1; afterwards 'docker image ls' still listed vlnab-b:run-bfd84ae1a6d1 (a dead run with no lease and no containers). New file in this sprint's change. From failure i18.
note: Root fix in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports: cleanup counted only containers labelled com.docker.compose.project=<tag> before removing a tag's artifacts. Added artifacts_in_use(docker, entry), which runs 'docker ps -a -q' with --filter ancestor=<image> per image, --filter volume=<name> per volume, and --filter network=<id> per network (same-key filters OR), and cleanup now skips a tag where has_containers or artifacts_in_use is true, so docker never sees an rm of an artifact a container (running or stopped, compose or plain 'docker run') uses, the DockerFailed conflict never ends the loop, and later dead tags are cleaned. New constant CONTAINER_FILTERS; the --help paragraph for cleanup now names the extra condition. free_stale's lease check keeps has_containers unchanged. Probed the new function against throwaway docker objects: stopped container on the image, a volume user, a running network user each read true, none read false. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports:cleanup -> :remove_artifacts -> :docker_out. What the code does: cleanup walks 'for tag in sorted(found)', skips a tag only where has_containers finds a container labelled com.docker.compose.project=<tag>, then remove_artifacts runs 'docker_out(docker, [kind, "rm", name], absent_ok=True)' for each image, volume, and network. docker_out raises DockerFailed for every stderr line DOCKER_ABSENT ('no such (image|volume|network)|network \S+ not found') does not match. Trigger: an image tagged run-<hex> (or a run's volume or network) still in use by a container that carries no compose label for that tag, such as a 'docker run' container an experiment started from the run's image, running or stopped; docker answers 'conflict: unable to remove repository reference ... is using its referenced image' (or 'volume is in use', 'has active endpoints'). Harm (A5): DockerFailed reaches the owner frame, which emits PORTS.RUN.FAILED and exits 1, and every tag sorted after the in-use one is never cleaned; that tag sorts at the same place on every later cleanup, so one in-use artifact stops every later cleanup from removing any other dead run's artifacts, while each drive and audit records a failed cleanup. decision:run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run Choice ('also removes the container artifacts ... of every run tag that holds no lease, has no containers left, and has no artifact made in the last hour') is not met for the other tags. Caused by the change (new code). Reports: i28.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md 'In drive mode' steps 2 and 4 and Loop 2 step 6; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review drive-command (fills only {name}, {folder}, {service}); plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/review/seed/project.md '## Drive commands' ('stack-start leases the run's ports with .ok-planner/bin/ports lease <run-tag> ... stack-stop ... ends the lease with .ok-planner/bin/ports release <run-tag>'). What the text does: this sprint's seed tells the owner to write stack-start and stack-stop around one run tag, but /converge runs them as two separate exec tasks, mints no tag (never calls .ok-planner/bin/run-tag), and hands none to either command or to the drivers; drive-command has no placeholder for it. Trigger: any drive with a stack, and two /converge runs in one checkout. Harm (A3): stack-stop cannot learn the tag stack-start leased and built under except from a fixed place the project invents, so it cannot release the lease or remove the run's artifacts by tag; with two runs at once, the second start overwrites that place and the first run's stop tears down the second's stack and releases its lease, the collision the story exists to prevent. Story concurrent-stacks-without-port-collisions; decision per-run-artifact-tag: 'A verification run invokes it once, builds every artifact it verifies under the printed tag, and hands that one value to its verification path'. Evidence: 'usage: review drive-command [-h] --role {...} [--name NAME] [--folder FOLDER] [--service SERVICE]'; grep -i 'run-tag|run tag' over skills/converge/ and scripts/review finds no line that mints or passes a tag. In scope: the seed's <run-tag> wording is this sprint's change. From failure i16.
note: scripts/review drive-command gains a {tag} placeholder (DRIVE_PLACEHOLDER_VALUES 'tag': run-[0-9a-f]{12}) and a --tag option; a command that names {tag} refuses without --tag, and --tag passed to a command that names none is accepted unchanged (DRIVE_PLACEHOLDERS_PASSED_UNNAMED), so existing stack lines without {tag} keep working (preserve). The placeholder refusal now reads 'does not match <pattern>', true for the tag's length too. skills/converge/SKILL.md drive step 2 mints the stack's tag with .ok-planner/bin/run-tag and passes it via --tag to stack-start; step 4 passes the same tag to stack-stop; Loop 2 step 6 mints a fresh tag for the confirm stack and stops with it. review/seed/project.md Drive commands names {tag} for stack-start and stack-stop and writes ports lease/release {tag}. Each run's start and stop now share a tag no other run holds, so stop releases its own lease and removes its own artifacts. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/review/seed/project.md

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md 'In drive mode' step 2 ('Where it fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds') and Loop 2 step 6 (confirm starts the stack and says nothing of a failed start). What the text does: a stack start that fails jumps to Loop 2 and skips step 4, the only place the run files stack-stop, the instance and resource stops, and the port cleanup this sprint added. Trigger: a stack-start that leased its ports and built its images, then failed (a failed health check, a bind failure past the retry budget). Harm (A8): decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run: 'The run's stack stop removes everything the run built under its tag, whether the run passed or failed'; the seed facts repeat it. The failed run's lease and artifacts stay, artifacts other than containers stay for good, and the run runs no cleanup, contrary to this sprint's work item 'file and drain one exec task running .ok-planner/bin/ports cleanup wherever review drive-stack printed stack'. Evidence: SKILL.md:77 step 2 quoted above; SKILL.md:79 step 4 holds the stop and the cleanup. In scope: the change added the cleanup to step 4 and the decision, and the failed-start path makes that outcome fail. From failure i20.
note: skills/converge/SKILL.md drive step 2: a failed stack start now runs step 4's stack stop (with the minted tag) and the port cleanup before going to Loop 2. Loop 2 step 6: a failed confirm start is named in the return with its unconfirmed defects, files no confirm driver, and stops the stack with its tag and runs the cleanup as step 4 does. review/seed/project.md tells the owner that stack-stop runs after a failed start too, so it must stop and remove a partly started stack. The failed run's lease and artifacts are removed, as decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run says. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/review/seed/project.md

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/drive.md and scripts/review drives: drivers on the shared stack get no run tag in their brief, so a service-log or sign-in command that must address the stack by its tag (a container stack runs as the compose project the tag names) cannot be written; the seed now gives {tag} to stack-start and stack-stop alone. Harm (A3): a driver cannot read the shared stack's service logs where the project names them by compose project. Fix would carry the stack's tag into the drive briefs and let drive.md pass --tag.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:stripped (called by retired_section_files, which strip_story_sections, strip_decision_proofs, diagnose, and the retired-sections offers all read). What the code does: retired_section_files decodes the raw bytes ('raw.decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")') and stripped splits on '(?<=
)' and tests 'heading = line.rstrip("
")' against '## <name>'. In a file with CRLF line endings each heading line is '## Proof', so no heading matches, found stays empty, and the file is skipped. At the base, strip_story_sections read the file through read_owner (open(path, encoding="utf-8"), universal newlines) and re.sub(r"
## (Falsifier|Proof|Acceptance)
.*?(?=
## |\Z)", ...) stripped the section from a CRLF file too (git show 119169e:./plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge, lines 3069-3100). Trigger: true-up or diagnose over a tracked, clean story or decision file with CRLF line endings holding a retired ## Falsifier, ## Proof, or ## Acceptance section. Harm (R4, unlisted behavior change; B133/B135 do not list it): old outcome, the section stripped; new outcome, the section kept with no diagnose finding and no retired-sections offer, so the owner is never told, against ADMINISTRATION.md 'Falsifier and story-proof elimination' and decision:whole-file-ownership. Caused by the change (W28 rewrote the strip). Reports: i24.
note: true-up::stripped now matches a heading with line.rstrip('\r\n'), so '## Proof\r' matches, and the seam collapse counts trailing/leading line breaks with (?:\r?\n)+ regexes (new TRAILING_BREAKS, LEADING_BREAKS, seam_breaks) and writes back the line ending it found, so a CRLF story or decision file is stripped and keeps its CRLF bytes; retired_section_files, strip_removable, retired_layout_offers, and diagnose all read through stripped. ADMINISTRATION.md 'Falsifier and story-proof elimination' says a heading matches with either ending. Driven on a scratch project: diagnose named the CRLF story, true-up stripped it, od shows CRLF kept. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:offers (the 'config_held = config_offers(); if not config_held: out.extend(port_range_offer())' branch) and port_range_offer (returns [] when .ok-planner/config.json is absent); ADMINISTRATION.md port-range row ('Withheld while a config, config-key, or citation-tags offer stands'). What the code does: it prints no port-range offer while any config, config-key, or citation-tags offer stands, and none at all while the config file is absent. Trigger: a project whose compose file publishes host ports and whose owner declines (or has not yet taken) the citation-tags offer; a declined offer returns on every true-up, so the port-range offer never appears. Harm (A3): the owner is never asked for a range, and .ok-planner/bin/ports lease then refuses with 'declare the names and a port_range through /ok', pointing the user at /ok, which never asks; the user cannot lease ports at all. Decision port-range-chosen-at-true-up: 'Where a project publishes ports and declares no provisioning range, the true-up core offers one.' The implementation notes' withholding ruling assumed the port-range offer 'appears on the second diagnose that /ok step 6.4 runs in the same pass', which holds only when the citation-tags offer is accepted. body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports:cleanup, has_containers, remove_artifacts. What the code does: has_containers(docker, tag) counts only containers labeled com.docker.compose.project=<tag>, so a run tag whose image a plain 'docker run' container uses (running or exited) counts as container-less; remove_artifacts then runs 'docker image rm', which the daemon refuses, docker_out raises DockerFailed, and the raise ends cleanup's 'for tag in sorted(found)' loop. Trigger: any container outside compose that uses an image tagged run-<12 hex>. Harm (A5): the periodic cleanup stops at that tag on every run for as long as the container exists, and no dead tag that sorts after it is ever cleaned, while the command looks like it works for earlier tags; decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run says the cleanup removes the artifacts of every run tag that 'has no containers left'. Evidence: stderr '{"kind": "PORTS.RUN.FAILED", "error": "DockerFailed", "message": "docker image rm vlnab-a:run-bcbf45ff2db7 exited 1: ... conflict: unable to delete ... container f6c6a9cccd88 is using its referenced image ..."}', exit 1; afterwards 'docker image ls' still listed vlnab-b:run-bfd84ae1a6d1 (a dead run with no lease and no containers). New file in this sprint's change. From failure i18.
note: Walked the trigger through ports:cleanup (471): a plain docker run container on a run-tagged image now makes artifacts_in_use (386) read true via 'ps -a -q --filter ancestor=<image>', so the tag is skipped before remove_artifacts and the DockerFailed conflict no longer ends the sorted loop; volumes and networks are checked the same way, -a covers stopped containers, per-kind calls keep same-key filters ORed. 'docker ps --filter ancestor=<missing image>' exits 0 empty here, so the check adds no raise of its own. free_stale keeps has_containers. Help text agrees with decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run ('no containers left'). Lint clean, py_compile ok, checks/run exit 0.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md 'In drive mode' steps 2 and 4 and Loop 2 step 6; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review drive-command (fills only {name}, {folder}, {service}); plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/review/seed/project.md '## Drive commands' ('stack-start leases the run's ports with .ok-planner/bin/ports lease <run-tag> ... stack-stop ... ends the lease with .ok-planner/bin/ports release <run-tag>'). What the text does: this sprint's seed tells the owner to write stack-start and stack-stop around one run tag, but /converge runs them as two separate exec tasks, mints no tag (never calls .ok-planner/bin/run-tag), and hands none to either command or to the drivers; drive-command has no placeholder for it. Trigger: any drive with a stack, and two /converge runs in one checkout. Harm (A3): stack-stop cannot learn the tag stack-start leased and built under except from a fixed place the project invents, so it cannot release the lease or remove the run's artifacts by tag; with two runs at once, the second start overwrites that place and the first run's stop tears down the second's stack and releases its lease, the collision the story exists to prevent. Story concurrent-stacks-without-port-collisions; decision per-run-artifact-tag: 'A verification run invokes it once, builds every artifact it verifies under the printed tag, and hands that one value to its verification path'. Evidence: 'usage: review drive-command [-h] --role {...} [--name NAME] [--folder FOLDER] [--service SERVICE]'; grep -i 'run-tag|run tag' over skills/converge/ and scripts/review finds no line that mints or passes a tag. In scope: the seed's <run-tag> wording is this sprint's change. From failure i16.
note: scripts/review drive-command: {tag} added to DRIVE_PLACEHOLDER_VALUES with run-[0-9a-f]{12}, --tag option added; drove it in a scratch project: stack-start naming {tag} fills it, refuses without --tag and on a malformed tag; a stop line without {tag} accepts --tag unchanged, so existing project.md lines keep working (release boundary held). converge SKILL.md drive step 2 mints via .ok-planner/bin/run-tag and passes it to stack-start, step 4 passes the same tag to stack-stop, Loop 2 step 6 mints a fresh tag for the confirm stack and stops with it. Seed project.md names {tag} for both stack roles and ports lease/release {tag}. Only callers of drive-command are converge SKILL.md and prompts/drive.md (drivers get no tag, as the seed says). Lint clean on the three files; checks/run all passed.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up 'if mode == "amend"' and resolve kind config, with ADMINISTRATION.md's 'amend draft' bullet (:270) and 'config' drafting entry (:120). What the code does: amend runs config_defects(draft) and refuses any lint-config draft config-check flags, and plumbline::portsDefects now flags the retired object form of ports; resolve config:<path> refuses a draft carrying any config-check defect, the retired form among them. ADMINISTRATION.md:270 tells the audit: 'A lint-config draft also converts a retired object form of ports to the array of its names ... since amend refuses a draft config-check flags'. Neither the audit's amend draft nor the config offer carries the line port_range_offer prints ('the retired .ok-planner/bin/port-block reads the retired object form for the caller(s) of intake issue(s) ...; converting ports to the array of its names ends its read-back'); planner_port_block_issues is read only in port_range_offer. Trigger: a trued-up project keeps its stack-start calling .ok-planner/bin/port-block (caller issue open, keep option chosen), declines the port-range offer, and accepts an audit amend draft for an unrelated ignore, tests, or folders finding, or a config offer for another defect. Harm (R2, B1 ruling migrate: the retired copy 'stays and keeps working while the issue stands', and 'the port-range offer says when converting the config ends its read-back'; B3: 'the port-range offer converts it on the owner's yes'): the unrelated draft converts ports silently, and the next stack-start fails with base port-block::main's refusal 'ports must be an object mapping each NAME ...' (git show 119169e:./plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/port-block), though the caller issue's keep option told the owner the copy keeps working. Caused by the change (B3's new config-check defect with amend's existing refusal). Reports: i29.
note: draft_config_defects drops the ports defects only when the draft's object-form ports equals the file's (json_value); amend and resolve config both use it. config_offers lists only non-ports defects and names only their keys in keep, so changed_keys refuses a ports change. Drove a scratch project: object ports + bad tests gives a config offer listing only tests; resolve refuses a draft converting ports (ports changed) and writes one keeping it; amend refuses a draft changing the object form, writes an unrelated ignore draft keeping it. Callers of config_offers/keep unchanged otherwise. ADMINISTRATION.md amend, config, config-check, and audit amend-draft text agree with the code. Lint and checks/run pass.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:offers (the 'config_held = config_offers(); if not config_held: out.extend(port_range_offer())' branch) and port_range_offer (returns [] when .ok-planner/config.json is absent); ADMINISTRATION.md port-range row ('Withheld while a config, config-key, or citation-tags offer stands'). What the code does: it prints no port-range offer while any config, config-key, or citation-tags offer stands, and none at all while the config file is absent. Trigger: a project whose compose file publishes host ports and whose owner declines (or has not yet taken) the citation-tags offer; a declined offer returns on every true-up, so the port-range offer never appears. Harm (A3): the owner is never asked for a range, and .ok-planner/bin/ports lease then refuses with 'declare the names and a port_range through /ok', pointing the user at /ok, which never asks; the user cannot lease ports at all. Decision port-range-chosen-at-true-up: 'Where a project publishes ports and declares no provisioning range, the true-up core offers one.' The implementation notes' withholding ruling assumed the port-range offer 'appears on the second diagnose that /ok step 6.4 runs in the same pass', which holds only when the citation-tags offer is accepted. Evidence: driver's scratch run printed only 'CLEANUP OFFERED (ok-planner): citation-tags:.ok-planner/config.json' and 'review-facts:...' on two true-ups while 'plumbline compose-ports' listed stack/compose.yaml:5 port 8080 and :9 DB_PORT; port-range appeared only after 'true-up resolve citation-tags:...'. New code in this sprint's change. From failure i15.
note: offers() now extends config_offers() and port_range_offer() unconditionally; port_range_offer reads {} where no config exists and still returns [] while a non-ports config-check defect stands. Drove a scratch project: no config + compose port shows citation-tags and port-range together; config with checks shows config-key, citation-tags, and port-range, the port-range Draft line dropping checks; a port-range draft written before citation-tags resolve is refused by the new dropped_citations with a draft-again message, so no whole-file draft silently drops the tags. amend with no file keeps current=None (no refusal change). ADMINISTRATION.md port-range row, drafting entry, and amend refusal list agree. Lint and checks/run pass.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md 'In drive mode' steps 2 and 4 and Loop 2 step 6; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review drive-command (fills only {name}, {folder}, {service}); plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/review/seed/project.md '## Drive commands' ('stack-start leases the run's ports with .ok-planner/bin/ports lease <run-tag> ... stack-stop ... ends the lease with .ok-planner/bin/ports release <run-tag>'). What the text does: this sprint's seed tells the owner to write stack-start and stack-stop around one run tag, but /converge runs them as two separate exec tasks, mints no tag (never calls .ok-planner/bin/run-tag), and hands none to either command or to the drivers; drive-command has no placeholder for it. Trigger: any drive with a stack, and two /converge runs in one checkout. Harm (A3): stack-stop cannot learn the tag stack-start leased and built under except from a fixed place the project invents, so it cannot release the lease or remove the run's artifacts by tag; with two runs at once, the second start overwrites that place and the first run's stop tears down the second's stack and releases its lease, the collision the story exists to prevent. Story concurrent-stacks-without-port-collisions; decision per-run-artifact-tag: 'A verification run invokes it once, builds every artifact it verifies under the printed tag, and hands that one value to its verification path'. Evidence: 'usage: review drive-command [-h] --role {...} [--name NAME] [--folder FOLDER] [--service SERVICE]'; grep -i 'run-tag|run tag' over skills/converge/ and scripts/review finds no line that mints or passes a tag. In scope: the seed's <run-tag> wording is this sprint's change. From failure i16.
note: confirm drive: reviewed skill:converge again (SKILL.md drive steps 2-4, Loop 2 step 6, prompts/drive.md, seed project.md, scripts/review drive-command) and ran drive-command in a scratch project (true-up, Drive commands naming {tag}). The stack half is fixed: step 2 mints with .ok-planner/bin/run-tag, steps 2/4 and Loop 2 step 6 pass --tag to stack-start and stack-stop; drive-command filled 'docker compose -p run-0d1a59d4599d ...' for start and stop, refused 'the stack-start command names {tag}; pass --tag' and "--tag 'run-XYZ' does not match run-[0-9a-f]{12}" (exit 1). Saw: the defect's other half stands. The defect says /converge 'hands none to either command or to the drivers'; the drivers still get neither the tag nor the leased ports. review drives puts no tag in a brief, prompts/drive.md tells a driver to call drive-command 'with --name, --folder, or --service' only, and grep -i port over drive.md finds nothing; the seed now says of {tag} 'no other role is given it'. So a driver of run A can reach its own stack's leased ports only through a fixed place the project invents, which run B's start overwrites, and run A's drivers then drive run B's stack: the story's harm ('one verification run never disturbs another's results'), and decision per-run-artifact-tag's 'hands that one value to its verification path through one environment variable the project declares' is still unmet for the verification path. Also: drive-command fills {tag} into service-log when --tag is passed ('docker compose -p run-0d1a59d4599d logs web', exit 0) contrary to the seed's 'no other role is given it', and a driver, given no --tag, gets 'the service-log command names {tag}; pass --tag' (exit 1).
