body: Reviewed /converge sprint mode's pass prompt against a scratch repo (git init; project root app/ trued up; code in app/main.py, shared/util.py, tools/gen.js; .ok-planner/config.json folders ["../shared","../tools"] written through true-up amend). review changed --base HEAD from app/ lists '../shared/util.py' and '../tools/gen.js', as the decision requires. sprint-pass.md line 17 tells a freshly dispatched pass agent to read 'each file's diff from `git diff --relative [BASE] -- <path>`'. --relative restricts git's output to the current directory, so for every file under a declared folder the diff is empty. Its sibling sprint-review.md line 20 says 'git diff [BASE] -- <path>' with no --relative. The story promises: 'so that no check the suite runs over my project misses code I own'; decision project-declares-its-folders: 'Every tool that lists or scopes the project's code reads that list: the review tool in every /converge mode'. saw: a reissued sprint-pass agent following the text reads no change for code in declared folders (and in a sprint's '## Paths outside the project root'). evidence: from app/: 'git diff --relative HEAD -- ../shared/util.py' printed nothing (exit 0, 0 lines); 'git diff HEAD -- ../shared/util.py' printed 'diff --git a/shared/util.py b/shared/util.py ... +# new narration line'; 'git diff --relative HEAD -- main.py' printed the diff for the root file.
note: sprint-pass-diff-skips-declared-folders

body: Reviewed the sprint template's Completion contract (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:239-270) against /converge sprint's closing step (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:119) and drove the mechanical steps on a scratch project (true-up, a scratch sprint with -base.txt, review changed/checks/merges/fixes/verifies/backouts, a stuck defect whose backout restores a lint failure). The story promises: "done" means the same thing for every sprint. Saw: the contract gives two verdicts for one repository state. Item 2 (sprint-document.md:249-250) reads "The project builds, and the checks .ok-planner/review/config.json lists under checks pass on every file the change touched." Certification's last step (converge/SKILL.md:119) reads "A file that fails now becomes a stuck defect with the check's output, and the loop does not reopen." The goal rule (sprint-document.md:259-263) reads both "The goal is met when items 1-3 verify against the repository as it stands" and "A stuck defect listed in the return is the owner's to take up, and does not hold the goal open." A sprint whose certification ends with a stuck check failure (or any stuck defect whose backout leaves a check failing) fails item 2 and is, by the stuck clause, not held open: one checker reports done, another not done. Decision sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository's Choice repeats the stuck clause and names no exception to item 2. Evidence: scratch run, final check exec "closed t2 failed (exit 2)" with "plumbline/comment-hygiene: comment is not permitted" on src/calc.py:6 before the fix; defect i4 set stuck and backout t7 filed with brief "defect i4; fix tasks t5; before: src/calc.py 7d0077a".
note: sprint-contract-stuck-check-two-verdicts

body: Reviewed /plan-sprint's issue walk and ran the script it calls against a scratch project (git init + true-up, design corpus with concept:widget, story:frobnicate-widgets, decision:blue-widgets). Filed issue pas-cites with artifacts [story:frobnicate-widgets, decision:blue-widgets, concept:widget] and ran 'OK_PLANNER_PROJECT_ROOT="$(pwd)" python3 .ok-planner/scripts/surface-corpus pas-cites' exactly as SKILL.md's walk says. The skill promises (SKILL.md 'The issue walk'): 'The script reads the record through the intake's module and prints, one per line, the concept, story, and decision files cited in its artifacts list'; the story promises the open design questions that bear on the owner's goals are resolved with the owner, and the walk is how the owner sees the bearing corpus (decision:relevance-scoped-queue-gate: 'walked with the owner — one at a time, with the corpus artifacts relevant to each surfaced first'). Saw: the decision and the concept print, the cited story never does. Evidence (exit 0): '.ok-planner/design/decisions/blue-widgets.md	decision	cited in the issue's artifacts' / '.ok-planner/design/concepts/widget.md	concept	cited in the issue's artifacts' and no line for the story, though '.ok-planner/design/stories/frobnicate-widgets.md' exists. An issue citing only story:frobnicate-widgets (pas-held) printed nothing at all, which SKILL.md tells the session to read as 'the issue is either about pure code with no corpus commitment or about a concept the record failed to name'. body: I reviewed /audit (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md) and the measurement auditor prompt it reads (skills/_shared/implementation-auditor.md, the story and assumption auditors) against the story and run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run. audit/SKILL.md, Port cleanup, says: `It frees and removes only what is due; an experiment's own stack stop removes what its run built.` The auditor prompt never tells an auditor or an experiment to build under a run tag, to stop a stack it starts, or to remove what it built: under `Obtaining the deployment state an experiment needs` it says `3. **Provision a second deployment** only when neither works` and gives no step that tears that deployment down; `grep -n -i 'run tag\|run-tag\|stack stop\|teardown'` over implementation-auditor.md finds no instruction of the kind (its only `teardown` is `the project's own teardown` used to reset). The decision says: `A run's artifacts end with the run: the run tag's life is mint, build, verify, remove`, and names the audit's experiment runs as runs whose artifacts the cleanup must reach. The audit runs `ports cleanup` once, right after the measurement track drains, when everything its experiments built is inside the hour of grace, so nothing a provisioned deployment of this audit built is removed by this run: container artifacts wait for a later cleanup, and other artifacts stay for good.
note: audit-experiments-leave-provisioned-deployments

Evidence (grep after the last true-up): '49:   core ( under ,'; '42:   intake () or in .' (the retired markdown intake the markdown-intake offer moved away); '75:   review --agent ok-opus --key <stage> --after <the build task>' (per-stage review tasks, which the current shape files none of); '149:    the closing  step being unrunnable for you'; '161:    running  with this sprint's path as its argument,'; '208:   divergences, and carries 's presentation'. ls .claude/skills/ after true-up: '_converge _shared _sprint _tasks audit converge dashboard discover-design document ok-version plan-sprint sketch triage-issues tupe-deploy' (no certify-work); ls .claude/skills/_shared/: no certification-core.md. An executor of the approved sprint is sent to a removed verb and a removed file, and no offer or diagnose line tells the owner.

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md (with plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md and the true-up core it drives) against the story; read the installed plugin registry read-only. The story promises: one deliberate act brings the project's whole suite presence to the current suite version; the skill's own opening says 'One command brings the suite current in this project: update the installed user-scoped plugins, ... then administer it in one pass'. Saw: step 1 runs 'claude plugin update <name>@ok-plugins   # for each installed ok-plugin, including ok itself', and step 4 then drives every core call from '<payload>', which 'Resolving the payload' fixes as '${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-plugins/ok}/families/ok-planner'. The installed front door lives at a versioned path: ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json reads 'ok@ok-plugins ... "installPath": "/Users/patrick/.claude/plugins/cache/ok-plugins/ok/25.4.0", "version": "25.4.0"'. An update installs the new release at a new versioned path, while the running session's CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT still names the old one until /reload-plugins, so the same pass trues the project up from the payload the update just superseded, and the report's carried column shows the old version. The skill tells the owner only 'Plugin updates take effect after /reload-plugins or a session restart', and never that the project was trued up to the pre-update version and needs /ok again after the reload (or that the pass must stop after step 1 when anything moved). Where the update removes the old cache folder, the step 4 commands name a payload that no longer exists. Either way one /ok does not bring the project to the current suite version whenever step 1 updates ok.
note: ok-trues-up-from-superseded-payload

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/SKILL.md: the phase 2 reviewer's thin-discovery request format is concept-only ('### <affected-concept-slug>', '- Promote new concept: <name | none>', SKILL.md:543-546), while the back-edge extractor is written for any kind ('Each names the affected artifact kind and slug', SKILL.md:675-676; it edits a story's statement or a decision's Choice) and speaks of 'Promote new artifact' (SKILL.md:670-671); the orchestrator fills the request between them, so a concept promotion still reaches the extractor, but no thin story or decision can be requested. Reading 1: the story promises only autonomous extraction into the catalogs, so a concept-only back-edge is enough. Reading 2: the extractor's own text shows the back-edge is meant to sharpen stories and decisions too, so the reviewer's format should name a kind and the field should read the same on both sides. The story bootstrap-design-corpus does not say which.
note: discover-design-back-edge-kinds

body: Reviewed the discover-design skill source (SKILL.md, the artifact-definitions and dispatch-discipline blocks it transcludes) and ran its scripts against a scratch project trued up from the working tree: issues list, issues file --from - (kind discover; a duplicate open id refused with exit 2), issues list --artifact, issues show --json, python3 .ok-planner/bin/catalog-toc and --check, and the step 9 archive moves (git mv for a tracked note, mv for an untracked one, rmdir of the emptied _discover/). All of that works. The divergence is in the back-edge's hand-off format. The phase 2 reviewer writes each thin discovery request as '### <affected-concept-slug>' with the field '- Promote new concept: <name | none>' (SKILL.md:543-546). The back-edge extractor is told 'add a new artifact file only where the original request authorized "Promote new artifact"' (SKILL.md:669-671) and that each request 'names the affected artifact kind and slug' (SKILL.md:675-676), and it edits 'a story's Story statement; a decision's Choice, Rationale, or Alternatives' (SKILL.md:683-686). The reviewer's format never names a kind or carries a 'Promote new artifact' field, so a story or decision cannot be the target of a request, and a literal reading of the extractor finds no authorization for a concept the reviewer asked to promote. The story promises: the as-is model extracted autonomously into durable catalogs, with owner attention spent only on genuine ambiguities. Saw: the one back-edge that sharpens thin artifacts cannot target stories or decisions, and its promotion field is named differently on the two sides, so a load-bearing artifact the reviewer flagged as thin stays thin or unwritten. Evidence: SKILL.md:546 'Promote new concept: <name | none>'; SKILL.md:670-671 'only where the original request authorized "Promote new artifact"'; SKILL.md:675-676 'Each names the affected artifact kind and slug'.
note: discover-design-back-edge-kinds

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports:run_artifacts takes an image as a run's only when its tag is exactly run-<12 hex> or its repository starts with the run tag, so an image tagged run-<12 hex>-amd64 (a suffixed run tag) is never removed, while the cleanup reports the run as removed. Reading 1: 'every image tagged with the run tag' (sprint work item; ports --help) means the exact tag, and a project that suffixes the tag builds outside the rule. Reading 2: decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run ('removes the container artifacts ... of every run tag') and the rules layer, which never says an image tag must equal the run tag, cover any tag that carries the run tag, so suffixed tags (seen on this machine: 28 images of another project, e.g. gridiq-allinone:run-d61aae7a593d-amd64, 6.24GB) should be removed too; widening the match also widens what a cleanup may delete across projects on the machine. Neither the story nor the decision decides it.
note: ports-cleanup-suffixed-run-tags

body: In the same scratch project I minted T3=run-62dc11c74373 and built one image under it with two tags, `docker build -t vlnab-arch:$T3-amd64 -t vlnab-plain:$T3`, then ran `.ok-planner/bin/ports cleanup` with the docker shim (two hours shifted, rm passed through for T3 only). The story promises: each run's artifacts are removed once the run is over; the rules layer (ok-planner-cheatsheet.md, Per-run artifacts) tells the owner to build every artifact a run verifies under its tag, and says cleanup removes the container artifacts of every dead run tag; it never says an image tag must equal the run tag exactly. Saw: cleanup printed `removed: run-62dc11c74373 (1 image(s), 0 volume(s), 0 network(s))`, reporting the run cleaned, yet `vlnab-arch:run-62dc11c74373-amd64` stayed: run_artifacts() takes an image only when its tag matches ^run-[0-9a-f]{12}$ whole or its repository starts with the run tag. On this machine `docker image ls` lists 28 images of another project tagged this way (`gridiq-allinone:run-d61aae7a593d-amd64` 6.24GB, `gridiq-grafana:run-d61aae7a593d-amd64` 992MB, `gridiq-keycloak:run-1a556e12fd9a-amd64` 247MB, ...), two to four weeks old; my shimmed cleanup listed none of them as due (no WOULD-REMOVE line), and a probe of run_artifacts() returned only my own tags. Evidence: the `removed:` line above; `docker image ls` after the cleanup: `vlnab-arch:run-62dc11c74373-amd64`; `docker system df`: Images 34.71GB, 16.91GB reclaimable. Possible not-owed reading for the merge: `ports --help` says `each image tagged with the run tag`, which an owner could read as exact; the rules layer an agent wires the stack from does not say it.
note: ports-cleanup-suffixed-run-tags

body: Sprint certification's alignment pass reports a delta not landed (C3), and plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md 'In sprint mode' step 5 and prompts/merge.md route every corpus fix to judgment, so certification cannot land the sprint's own approved delta; contract item 1 ('Every corpus matches every delta above, applied verbatim') then stays unmet, and the goal rule exempts only a stuck defect, so a goal checker either loops or ignores item 1. Reading 1: landing an approved sprint's own delta verbatim is a change 'through a sprint's deltas', which the decision allows, so certification's fixer may land it. Reading 2: the decision's 'A defect whose fix lies in the corpus ... goes to the intake as a judgment issue' binds every /converge run, so the contract's goal rule must exempt a judgment item as it exempts a stuck one. The corpus does not decide which.
note: certification-cannot-land-its-own-delta

body: Reviewed /converge sprint mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, prompts/sprint-pass.md, prompts/merge.md) against the sprint template's Completion contract (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:239-270); ran review owner on a scratch project, which classes the sprint's own applied delta .ok-planner/design/stories/subtract-numbers.md as "corpus". The story promises: when a sprint closes, the owner knows whether what was approved was delivered, and "done" means the same thing for every sprint. Saw: certification finds an unlanded delta and cannot land it, and the contract then has no outcome. The alignment pass reports C3 "A corpus delta whose artifact ... does not match the delta's final-form body byte for byte" (_sprint/shared.md:276). converge/SKILL.md:103 then routes it away from the fix loop: "it applies the ownership test of merge step 3a to the file each fix lies in, as in every mode, even where the sprint's change edited the file or a delta names the artifact: a fix in the corpus or the harness settings sets the item to judgment" (same in prompts/merge.md:62). Contract item 1 (sprint-document.md:244-248) requires "Every corpus matches every delta above, applied verbatim", and the goal rule exempts only a stuck defect. A judgment item is not stuck, so the goal stays unmet with nothing left in the run to meet it, and a /goal checker either loops or a reader ignores item 1. Decision runs-fix-what-the-project-owns says the corpus changes "only through a sprint's deltas", which a verbatim landing of this sprint's own delta is. Evidence: "corpus\t.ok-planner/design/stories/subtract-numbers.md" from review owner in the scratch project.
note: certification-cannot-land-its-own-delta
